rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 7 (58.1734; oval 63.49, s-bend 66.85, slalom 44.19; no completions). Iterations 7 and 8 gave identical scores to four decimals while kd, wheel_track and base_speed changed, so those controller values have no measurable effect in this regime. The round-1 critique is right that my draft was confounded: it changed kd, wheel_track, kp, mass and sensor_size at once, and it stated a baseline that had never raced. Its kd 1.5 is also unsupported, because the loop gives 100*kd per unit of signal change per step.

What I kept: the raced iteration 7 controller (kp 4.5, ki 0, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.5, linear weights, last_direction), the sensor row at y 0.08 with x from -0.03 to +0.03 at 0.01 m spacing, wheel_track 0.12 and mass 0.8. What I rejected: kd 1.5, wheel_track 0.14 to 0.16, kp 3.0, mass 0.6 and the ±0.06 m span, all of which are unraced or were confounded. Iteration 9 (±0.06 m span at 0.02 m spacing) scored 55.13, so that span is worse.

What I changed: one variable only, sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, with every other value as in iteration 7. The critique notes that 0.012 was never tested against 0.016 in this layout. A larger footprint keeps the sum of readings higher when a tape edge falls between sensors, which should reduce line-loss events. The 0.016 footprint overlaps neighbours more, so it may blur the edge reading. This race tests which effect dominates.

Falsifiable targets relative to 58.17: line_loss_events at or below 1 on the s-bend and slalom; oval line_loss_events at or below 2 and oval max_error below 0.06; progress at or above 0.16 on all tracks. Reversal rule: if the score falls below 58.17, or any track's max_error rises above its raced value, return sensor_size to 0.012 and keep the iteration 7 design as the fallback for the final stage.
